affected_system: food access, environmental health inspection, and community protection
alternatives: rank verified high-consequence candidates for food-access and environmental-health investment portfolio
select a risk-, equity-, and lifecycle-balanced portfolio for food-access and environmental-health investment portfolio
pair access-, risk-, equity-, and lifecycle portfolio optimization with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Food outlets, inspections, assistance, prices, access, and environmental complaints have separate semantics.
Area food access is not treated as individual diet, food security, or health outcome.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: fund only already-committed work for food-access and environmental-health investment portfolio.

constraints.description: The food access and environmental health prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: environmental health commissioner and food-access program director
decision_question: Which inspection, cold-chain, market, transportation, and assistance investments should be funded?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The food access and environmental health prioritize must respect declared capital, operating, maintenance, and delivery budgets.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for food-access and environmental-health investment portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: access-, risk-, equity-, and lifecycle portfolio optimization
independence_key.primary_outcome: population-weighted food and environmental service gap

intended_claim: A versioned prioritize design for comparing declared alternatives affecting food-access and environmental-health investment portfolio, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: population-weighted food and environmental service gap
distributional gap in population-weighted food and environmental service gap
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report modeled access improvement as better diet, health, or verified hazard reduction.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for food-access and environmental-health investment portfolio passes documented checks for cost, benefit, service life, dependencies, deliverability, and maintenance burden.

title: Prioritize food-access and environmental-health investments
transportability_risks: Retail markets, informal food systems, inspection law, mobility, prices, and eligibility vary.
Administrative participation can understate eligible need.
